1.s: The elder writes to his friend Gaius, praising his hospitality to travelling missionaries, warning about Diotrephes, “who loves to be first”, and commending Demetrius. “Don’t imitate that which is evil, but that which is good.”
1.d: A rare personal glimpse of conflict and kindness in an early church. “I have no greater joy than this, to hear about my children walking in truth.”
